documentation_gaps.description: The OGTT results are documented but the diagnostic criteria for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) are not explicitly stated. The 1-hour value of 9.2 mmol/L and 2-hour value of 7.8 mmol/L are elevated, but the chart does not specify which criteria were used (e.g., IADPSG/WHO) or whether the diagnosis is based on one or more abnormal values.
documentation_gaps.why_it_matters: Coding for GDM requires documentation of the specific diagnostic criteria or the abnormal values that support the diagnosis. Without this, the specificity of the diagnosis may be questioned, and the clinical accuracy of the diagnosis is not fully established.

documentation_gaps.description: The chart does not document the clinical correlation or planned workup for the abnormal OGTT results. Although the diagnosis of GDM is made, there is no explicit statement of the clinical significance or the follow-up plan beyond monitoring blood glucose.
documentation_gaps.why_it_matters: For CDI purposes, an abnormal lab value (OGTT) without explicit clinical correlation may be considered incomplete. The provider should clarify the clinical significance of the abnormal OGTT to ensure accurate coding and appropriate management.

specialist_trace.rationale: To ensure accurate coding, the chart must explicitly state the diagnostic criteria used (e.g., IADPSG/WHO) and confirm that the diagnosis is based on the specific number of abnormal OGTT values (e.g., one or two) per those criteria. Additionally, document the clinical correlation of the elevated 1-hour and 2-hour results with the GDM diagnosis, and specify the planned follow-up (e.g., frequency of glucose monitoring, target ranges, and referral to nutrition or endocrinology) to support the medical necessity of the encounter.

I do not have live PubMed search access, so I cannot provide verified PMIDs. However, based on established literature, the IADPSG/WHO 2013 criteria diagnose GDM if any single value meets or exceeds thresholds (fasting ≥5.1, 1h ≥10.0, 2h ≥8.5 mmol/L). Your patient’s values (1h 9.2, 2h 7.8) do **not** meet these cutoffs, so under IADPSG/WHO she would **not** be diagnosed with GDM—only under older Carpenter-Coustan or NDDG criteria (which use lower 2h thresholds, e.g., ≥7.8 mmol/L) would the 2h value alone qualify. Given the ambiguity, I recommend explicitly documenting the criteria used and, if IADPSG/WHO is applied, reclassifying her as having isolated elevated glucose without GDM, while still advising lifestyle modification and repeat testing given her risk profile.
